item.description:

SplitIterator

@memory_only
struct SplitIterator[is_mutable: Bool, //, origin: Origin[mut=is_mutable]]
Get an iterator the yields the splits from the input `to_split` string.
TODO: these test run fine in the test module, but not in doctests.
```
from std.testing import assert_equal
from extramojo.bstr.bstr import SplitIterator
var input = "ABCD EFGH IJKL

MNOP".as_bytes() var expected = List( “ABCD”.as_bytes(), “EFGH”.as_bytes(), “IJKL MNOP”.as_bytes() ) var output = ListSpan[UInt8, ImmStaticOrigin] for value in SplitIterator(input, ord(" “)): output.append(value) for i in range(len(expected)): assert_equal(StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=output[i]), StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=expected[i])) ```

```
from std.collections.string import StringSpan
from std.testing import assert_equal
from extramojo.bstr.bstr import SplitIterator
var input = "ABCD EFGH IJKL

MNOP”.as_bytes() var expected = List( “ABCD”.as_bytes(), “EFGH”.as_bytes(), “IJKL MNOP”.as_bytes() ) var iter = SplitIterator(input, ord(" “)) var first = iter.next() var peek = iter.peek() var second = iter.next() assert_equal(StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=peek.value()), StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=second)) assert_equal(StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=first), StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=expected[0])) assert_equal(StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=second), StringSpan(unsafe_from_utf8=expected[1])) ```

item.title: find
item.description:
Mojo function 🡭

find

➕  ➖ 
def find(haystack: Span[UInt8], needle: Span[UInt8]) -> Optional[Int]

Look for the substring needle in the haystack. This is not a terribly smart find implementation. It will use memchr to find occurrences of the first byte in the needle, it then checks the subsequent bytes to see if they match the rest of the needle.

from std.testing import assert_equal
from extramojo.bstr.bstr import find

var haystack = "ABCDEFGhijklmnop".as_bytes()
var expected = 4
var answer = find(haystack, "EFG".as_bytes()).value()
assert_equal(answer, expected)

Args:

  • haystack (Span[UInt8]): The bytes to be searched for the needle.
  • needle (Span[UInt8]): The bytes to search for in the haystack.

Returns:

Optional[Int]: Index of the start of the first occurrence of needle.

is_ascii_lowercase

➕  ➖ 
def is_ascii_lowercase(value: UInt8) -> Bool

Check if a byte is ASCII lowercase. 

from std.testing import assert_true, assert_false
from extramojo.bstr.bstr import is_ascii_lowercase

for ascii_letter in range(ord("A"), ord("Z")+1):
 assert_false(is_ascii_lowercase(ascii_letter))
for ascii_letter in range(ord("a"), ord("z")+1):
 assert_true(is_ascii_lowercase(ascii_letter))
assert_false(is_ascii_lowercase(0))

Args:

  • value (UInt8)

Returns:

Bool
